title: Cheapest Diwali Decoration Markets in India: Where to Buy Wholesale Across Cities
summary: Where to buy Diwali decorations at wholesale prices across India. Sadar Bazaar Delhi, Begum Bazaar Hyderabad, Burrabazar Kolkata and more.
body_markdown:
The diyas, LED strings, torans, rangoli stencils, artificial garlands and hanging lanterns that appear in retail shops across India every October do not materialise from nowhere. They move from a handful of wholesale markets in five or six cities to every neighbourhood store and street vendor in the country. Buying from those source markets rather than the retail endpoint is how families, event planners, housing society committees and small shopkeepers cut their Diwali decoration budget by 40 to 70 percent.


This guide maps the cheapest diwali decoration market india options, city by city, with what each market stocks and how the pricing works.


## **Why Wholesale Markets Price Differently**


A retail shop in a residential neighbourhood buys its Diwali stock from these wholesale markets, marks it up, and sells it to you. The wholesale market sells the same product at the price the retailer paid. The gap is not about quality. It is about how many hands the product passes through before it reaches the buyer.


# **Cheapest Diwali Decoration Markets Across India: City by City**


The markets below are genuine wholesale hubs. Retail buyers are welcome at all of them, though the best prices come with quantity.


## **Sadar Bazaar, Delhi**


Sadar Bazaar is the largest wholesale market in Delhi and arguably the single most important Diwali decoration source market in North India. The stalls near Swadeshi Market and along the lanes between Narain Market and the main bazaar road carry the highest concentration of festive stock.


**What it stocks:** Earthen diyas (from Rs 1 per piece in bulk), LED string lights, rice lights, fairy light curtains, decorative torans, bandhanwar, artificial marigold garlands, rangoli stencils and powder colours, door hangings, wall hangings, paper lanterns, designer candles, incense sets and Lakshmi Ganesh idol sets.


**Pricing context:** A string of 100 LED lights that retails for Rs 200 to Rs 300 in a neighbourhood store is available here for Rs 80 to Rs 120. Decorative torans that sell for Rs 150 retail are Rs 50 to Rs 70 wholesale.


**Timings:** 10:00 AM to 7:00 PM, Monday to Saturday. Closed Sundays, though Diwali week may see Sunday opening.


**Adjacent advantage:** Bhagirath Palace, the wholesale electrical market in Chandni Chowk, sits nearby and stocks heavy-duty LED installations, decorative bulbs and commercial-grade lighting.


## **Begum Bazaar, Hyderabad**


Begum Bazaar is Hyderabad’s oldest wholesale market, operating for over 200 years near Nampally station. During Diwali, the market transforms into a decoration wholesale hub serving the entire Telangana and Andhra Pradesh retail network.


**What it stocks:** Diyas, LED lighting, plastic and metal decorative items, gift wrapping supplies, artificial flowers, tinsel and Diwali-specific household items. The cosmetics section carries Diwali gift sets and beauty hampers at wholesale rates.


**Pricing context:** Prices run 30 to 50 percent below Hyderabad retail for identical items. The advantage is strongest on LED lights and plastic decorative items.


**Timings:** 10:00 AM to 8:00 PM. Closed Sundays.


## **Burrabazar, Kolkata**


Burrabazar (also written as Bara Bazaar) in north Kolkata is eastern India’s primary wholesale hub. The Diwali and Kali Puja decoration stock here serves retail networks across West Bengal, Bihar, Jharkhand and the northeast.


**What it stocks:** Decorative lighting, clay and terracotta diyas (Kolkata’s terracotta tradition produces painted and designer diyas that differ from the North Indian plain earthen variety), alpana (rangoli) materials, puja items for Kali Puja, and wholesale gift packaging.


**Pricing context:** The terracotta diya section is particularly competitive. Hand-painted designer diyas that retail for Rs 20 to Rs 30 per piece are available at Rs 5 to Rs 10 wholesale.


**Timings:** 10:00 AM to 7:00 PM. Closed Sundays.


## **Manek Chowk, Ahmedabad**


Manek Chowk serves a triple function. It is a jewellery market by day, a vegetable market by morning, and a street food market by night. During the Diwali and Navratri window, the wholesale section stocks decoration items that serve the Gujarat retail network.


**What it stocks:** Torans (which are culturally central in Gujarati Diwali celebrations), rangoli materials, diyas, Lakshmi Ganesh idol sets, decorative wall hangings and the specific Gujarati Diwali items like bandhanwar and shubh labh hangings.


**Pricing context:** The toran prices at Manek Chowk are among the lowest in the country because Gujarat’s Diwali tradition places torans at every doorway, creating the volume that drives wholesale pricing.


## **Chickpet, Bangalore**


Chickpet is Bangalore’s oldest commercial district. The Diwali stock here serves the Karnataka and parts of the Tamil Nadu retail network. The market sits near the Bangalore City railway station, making it accessible from most parts of the city.


**What it stocks:** Diyas, LED lighting, decorative items, puja materials, gift wrapping, plastic flowers and Diwali-specific home decor. The textile section carries festive fabric and readymade ethnic wear at wholesale adjacent pricing.


**Pricing context:** Prices run 25 to 40 percent below retail for decoration items. The LED lighting section is competitive with Delhi’s Bhagirath Palace for basic string lights.


## **What to Buy Where: Quick Reference**


**Product** **Best Source Market**


Earthen diyas, bulk Sadar Bazaar Delhi, Burrabazar Kolkata


Designer terracotta diyas Burrabazar Kolkata


LED string lights, wholesale Bhagirath Palace Delhi, Chickpet Bangalore


Torans and bandhanwar Manek Chowk Ahmedabad, Sadar Bazaar Delhi


Rangoli colours and stencils Sadar Bazaar Delhi


Gift wrapping and packaging Begum Bazaar Hyderabad, Burrabazar Kolkata


Lakshmi Ganesh idols Sadar Bazaar Delhi, Manek Chowk Ahmedabad


## **When to Buy**


The decoration stock appears in wholesale markets roughly 3 to 4 weeks before Diwali. The widest selection and the lowest prices are available 2 to 3 weeks before the festival. By the final week, popular items sell out at the busiest stalls and remaining stock commands less negotiable pricing.


For the best wholesale experience, visit on a weekday morning. Saturday afternoons at any of these markets during Diwali season are extremely crowded.


Prices are approximate and may vary based on season, demand, and availability.


## **Common Questions About Wholesale Diwali Decoration Shopping**


### **Which is the cheapest diwali decoration market india wide?**


Sadar Bazaar in Delhi and Burrabazar in Kolkata offer the lowest wholesale prices for Diwali decorations nationally.


### **Can retail buyers shop at wholesale Diwali markets?**


All the listed wholesale markets welcome retail buyers. Prices are lower than retail shops even for single-piece purchases.


### **Where can I buy wholesale LED lights for Diwali?**


Bhagirath Palace in Delhi and the Chickpet lighting section in Bangalore are the two strongest wholesale LED light sources.


### **How much cheaper are wholesale Diwali decorations than retail?**


Wholesale decoration prices run 40 to 70 percent below neighbourhood retail depending on the item and the quantity purchased.


### **What is the best time to buy Diwali decorations at wholesale?**


Visit 2 to 3 weeks before Diwali for the widest selection and strongest pricing. The final week sees sellouts and firmer rates.


### **Where can I buy designer diyas at wholesale prices?**


Burrabazar in Kolkata carries hand-painted terracotta designer diyas at Rs 5 to Rs 10 wholesale versus Rs 20 to Rs 30 retail.


### **Is Begum Bazaar good for Diwali decoration shopping?**


Begum Bazaar is Hyderabad’s primary wholesale source for Diwali decorations, LED lights, gift sets and household items at 30 to 50 percent below retail.


### **What are torans and where should I buy them for Diwali?**


Torans are decorative door hangings central to Gujarati Diwali tradition. Manek Chowk in Ahmedabad offers the lowest toran prices.


### **Can I buy rangoli materials at wholesale markets?**


Sadar Bazaar in Delhi carries rangoli powder colours, stencils, stickers and materials at wholesale rates throughout the Diwali season.


### **Are these markets open on Sundays during Diwali?**


Most wholesale markets close on Sundays normally. During Diwali week, some shops may open on Sunday but this varies by market.
